title: The sunspot-number fall near 1981 is also present in Locarno counts at matched emission
abstract: We test whether the sunspot-number fall near 1981 occurs in the international index relative to a station that observed across the production transfer. We use Locarno group records, SILSO V2, F10.7 and measured Mg II. On common observation days in November 1978 to June 1983, international sunspot number falls by 13.7% at matched F10.7 and 11.6% at matched Mg II. Its ratio to the Locarno weighted Wolf count changes by +1.7% and +1.6%, with conditional 95% intervals of about 0.989-1.044. A single-observer control gives +0.3% for both references. Local time slopes retain the absence of a large negative international-to-station change. An exact decomposition shows that the split between group count and weighted spots per group depends on the time model. A separate 14% fall in the international index with a stable station does not fit these models. This result does not prove a solar cause: Locarno anchors the index after 1981, and shared counting changes remain possible. External observations stay outside the publication.

display.caption: The international-to-station factor stays near or above one. The internal station decomposition depends on the time model. Intervals use six-month residual blocks and condition on each fitted model.
